title: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh, stewed, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Stewed chicken leg, drumstick and thigh without skin is a lean source of protein obtained by slow cooking in liquid. The method keeps the meat moist while the lack of skin reduces saturated fat content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken drumsticks and thighs contain more iron than breast meat.
Stewing preserves more B‑vitamins compared with frying.
Stewed chicken parts are staples in many Eastern European and Asian cuisines.
Cooking without skin dramatically lowers the cholesterol level of the dish.
Skin‑less chicken is easier to digest for people with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 20 g of complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron and zinc
items.content: These minerals support normal blood formation and immune function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Stewed chicken is rich in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Removing the skin cuts saturated fat, making it heart‑friendly.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: Protein combined with a modest amount of fat helps you feel full longer.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Chicken must be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 74 °C; undercooking can lead to salmonella.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt or ready‑made sauces can raise sodium levels, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Histamine formation
items.content: If stored too long, stewed meat can accumulate histamine, causing food intolerance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Stewed legs, drumsticks and thighs can be served as a main dish, added to soups, stews, salads, or used as a filling for pies. Any remaining small bits of fat can be trimmed before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags for up to 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 74 °C before eating.
